chunks.text: 49-year-old male, Professional, resident of Tampines, Singapore.
Right wrist fracture in 2008, fully healed
General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway (LMA)
General anesthesia for appendectomy in 2005, no complications

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your hernia surgery today. Let me go through some questions to make sure we're all set for your general anesthesia with the LMA. First, can you tell me a bit about your hernia and why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes. This hernia on my left side has been bulging for almost a year now. It doesn't hurt much, but it gets uncomfortable when I lift heavy things or bend over. My surgeon said it's better to fix it before it gets worse, so here I am.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for sharing that. Let's talk about your medications. I see you're on Metformin, Perindopril, Indapamide, and Atorvastatin. Are you still taking all of these as prescribed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, all of them except Amlodipine. I stopped that one about six months ago because my ankles kept swelling up. My GP said it was due to the Amlodipine, so we switched me off it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. The records mentioned Amlodipine was still active, so I appreciate you correcting that. Did you have any other side effects from it besides the swelling?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, just the swelling. Blood pressure's been fine since I stopped it, though. My BP readings at the clinic have been pretty stable lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to know. Any allergies we should be aware of?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: None at all. Never had any reactions to medications or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you eaten or drunk anything this morning? Remember, it's important to be NPO for surgery.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing since midnight. Just a sip of water to take my morning pills, like the nurse instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia experiences we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had my appendix out when I was a teenager, but that's it. No problems with the anesthesia then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Lastly, how's your overall fitness? Can you walk up a flight of stairs without getting short of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, no problem. I walk to the hawker center every day for lunch, and that's about 10 minutes. Only the hernia stops me from doing heavier stuff.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for all the details, Mr. Tan. I'll update your records about the Amlodipine and make sure the team knows. Any questions or concerns before we proceed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Just want to get this sorted and go back to my badminton games without pain lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Haha, sounds like a plan. We'll take good care of you. You'll meet the surgical team shortly, and I'll see you in the operating room.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] normal saline running at one hundred fifty milliliters per hour

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five, gave five hundred milligrams of intravenous fluid bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] mean arterial pressure improved to sixty five

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] heart rate increased to ninety five, gave ten milligrams of intravenous metoprolol

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, okay lah. Got some pain here, but manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you tell me your pain score out of 10? And where exactly is the discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 4 or 5? Around the incision site, like a dull ache.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? Breathing comfortably?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No vomiting, but feel a bit queasy. Throat a bit sore, but breathing okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Did you remember anything during the operation? Any awareness?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, slept like a baby. No memory at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: For your diabetes, did the team check your sugar levels? Any episodes of low or high?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: They checked before and after, all normal. No dizziness or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Your blood pressure and cholesterol meds—taken as usual?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, took them this morning before surgery. BP been stable, no issues.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, anything else bothering you? We can adjust pain relief if needed.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think it's all good. Thanks for checking.
